source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Incorporate frontline knowledge of patient acuity, care needs, and staff skills into staffing plans","B":"Exclude direct-care nurses from staffing decisions so planning remains entirely administrative","C":"Use one fixed staffing number for every shift without considering acuity, workload, or skill mix","D":"Transfer staffing decisions to personnel with no direct knowledge of unit-level patient-care demands"}}
source_row.rationale: ANA describes staffing committees as nurse-led groups that create unit-level staffing plans based on patient acuity and needs matched with staff skills and experience, and supports substantial direct-care nurse representation. Frontline input is therefore an intended safety feature of this model.
source_row.source_detail: Staffing committees: nurse-led groups create unit-level staffing plans based on patient population acuity/needs and staff skills/experience; ANA supports direct-care nurse representation.
source_row.source_name: American Nurses Association — Advocating for Safe Staffing in Nursing
source_row.stem: Why do nurse staffing committees include direct-care nurse representation?
